source_refs.note: Book p. 119-120: 3.8.3 definition box (average value), Example 70 and Example 71 (temperature sensor).

blocks.title: finition:
blocks.text: If \(f\) is continuous on \([a, b]\), then its average value on \([a, b]\) (also called its mean value) is \(f_{\text{av}} = \frac{1}{b-a}\int_a^b f(x)\,dx\).

blocks.title: Book correction
blocks.text: The heading of this box is printed cut off as "finition:"; it should read "Definition:".

blocks.title: Teaching note
blocks.text:
Why this formula? The average of \(n\) numbers is (their sum) \(\div n\). A continuous function has infinitely many values on \([a, b]\), so we replace the sum by the integral \(\int_a^b f(x)\,dx\) and the count \(n\) by the length \(b - a\) of the interval.
Picture: \(f_{\text{av}}\) is the height of the rectangle on \([a, b]\) whose area equals the area under the curve, \((b - a)\,f_{\text{av}} = \int_a^b f(x)\,dx\). The hills of the curve above this level fill the valleys below it.
Useful rearrangement: \(\int_a^b f(x)\,dx = (b - a)\,f_{\text{av}}\). Exercise 3.7 (Q8 to Q11) uses it.

blocks.title: Example 70
blocks.problem: Find the average value of the function \(f(x) = x^{2} + 2\) over the interval \([-1, 2]\).
steps:
Given: \(f(x) = x^{2} + 2\) on \([-1, 2]\).
To find: the average value \(f_{\text{av}}\).
Method: use the definition \(f_{\text{av}} = \frac{1}{b-a}\int_a^b f(x)\,dx\) with \(a = -1\), \(b = 2\); \(f\) is a polynomial, so it is continuous and the definition applies.

Set up the formula (as printed)
With \(a = -1\) and \(b = 2\), we have
\[f_{\text{av}} = \dfrac{1}{b-a}\int_a^b f(x)\,dx\]
\[= f_{\text{av}} = \dfrac{1}{2-(-1)}\int_{-1}^{2}(x^{2} + 2)\,dx\]
\[= \dfrac{1}{3}\left[\dfrac{x^{3}}{3} + 2x\right]_{-1}^{2}\]
Why: \(b - a = 2 - (-1) = 3\); the antiderivative of \(x^{2} + 2\) is \(\frac{x^{3}}{3} + 2x\).

Put in the limits
\[= \dfrac{1}{3}\left[\left(\dfrac{2^{3}}{3} + 2(2)\right) - \left(\dfrac{(-1)^{3}}{3} + 2(-1)\right)\right]\]
\[= \dfrac{1}{3}\left(\dfrac{8}{3} + \dfrac{1}{3} + 4 + 2\right)\]
\[= \dfrac{1}{3}\left(\dfrac{9}{3} + 6\right) = 3\]
Why: \((-1)^{3} = -1\), so subtracting \(-\frac{1}{3} - 2\) adds \(\frac{1}{3} + 2\).

Check:
\(f\) runs from its least value \(f(0) = 2\) to its greatest value \(f(2) = 6\) on \([-1, 2]\); the average 3 lies between them. Also \(f(x) = 3\) at \(x = \pm 1\), and \(x = 1\) lies in \([-1, 2]\), so \(f\) really takes its average value there.
blocks.answer: The average value of \(f(x) = x^{2} + 2\) over \([-1, 2]\) is 3.

blocks.title: Book correction
blocks.text: The book's first line writes \(f_{\text{av}} = \frac{1}{b-a}\int_a^b f(x)\,dx = f_{\text{av}} = \frac{1}{2-(-1)}\int_{-1}^{2}(x^{2}+2)\,dx\), with \(f_{\text{av}}\) repeated in the middle of the chain. It should read \(f_{\text{av}} = \frac{1}{b-a}\int_a^b f(x)\,dx = \frac{1}{2-(-1)}\int_{-1}^{2}(x^{2}+2)\,dx\). The answer 3 is correct.

blocks.title: Example 71
blocks.problem: A temperature sensor moves slowly along a 10-meter track, continuously measuring temperature. The temperature at position \(x\) is given by \(T(x) = 20 + x\), where \(T(x)\) is in \(^{\circ}\)C. Find the average temperature measured by the sensor as it moves from \(x = 0\) to \(x = 10\) meters.
steps:
Given: \(T(x) = 20 + x\) \(^{\circ}\)C for \(0 \le x \le 10\) m.
To find: the average temperature.
Method: the average of a continuous quantity along an interval is \(\frac{1}{b-a}\int_a^b T(x)\,dx\); here \(a = 0\), \(b = 10\).

Set up the average
Function: \(T(x) = 20 + x\); limits are from \(x = 0\) to \(x = 10\).
\[\text{Average Temperature} = \dfrac{1}{10 - 0}\int_{0}^{10}(20 + x)\,dx\]
Why: the sensor measures continuously, so we average with an integral instead of adding a few readings.

Integrate and evaluate
\[= \dfrac{1}{10}\left[20x + \dfrac{x^{2}}{2}\right]_{0}^{10}\]
\[= \dfrac{1}{10}\left[\left(20(10) + \dfrac{(10)^{2}}{2}\right) - \left(20(0) + \dfrac{(0)^{2}}{2}\right)\right]\]
\[= \dfrac{1}{10}(200 + 50) = 25\,^{\circ}\text{C}\]
Why: \(\int 20\,dx = 20x\) and \(\int x\,dx = \frac{x^{2}}{2}\).

Check:
\(T\) is linear, so its average is the mean of the end values: \(\frac{T(0) + T(10)}{2} = \frac{20 + 30}{2} = 25\).

blocks.title: Key points
blocks.text:
1. \(f_{\text{av}} = \frac{1}{b-a}\int_a^b f(x)\,dx\), for \(f\) continuous on \([a, b]\).
2. Equivalent form: \(\int_a^b f(x)\,dx = (b - a)\,f_{\text{av}}\).
3. The average lies between the least and greatest values of \(f\) on \([a, b]\).
4. For a straight-line function, the average is the mean of the two end values.

blocks.title: Common mistake
blocks.text:
1. Forgetting to divide by \(b - a\): the integral alone is an area, not an average.
2. Using \(b + a\) or \(a - b\): with \(a = -1\), \(b = 2\) the length is \(2 - (-1) = 3\).
3. Sign slips with a negative lower limit: \(\left(\frac{(-1)^{3}}{3} + 2(-1)\right) = -\frac{7}{3}\), and subtracting it adds \(\frac{7}{3}\).
